You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF at S1).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at S1; compare it with the
output window and the diode drops.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:

 "proposals": [

    },

      "out",

     ],

    },
    {

      "pzp",

     ],

    },
    {

      "n1",

     ],

    },
    {

     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

reply.reasoning:
*   Goal: $V_{out\_min} \ge 1.8\text{V}$, $V_{out\_max} \le 3.6\text{V}$, Ripple $\le 0.05\text{V}$, $T_{up} \le 0.4\text{s}$, Settled $\le 0.02\text{V}$.
    *   Current best: `SSHI` (topology `40eae91a637a`).
        *   Passed 5/6 conditions.
        *   Only failure: S3 ripple (0.06398V > 0.05V).
        *   S3 is the "strong excitation, light load" case ($I_p = 100\text{uA}$, $R_L = 2.2\text{M}\Omega$).
    *   `Symmetric_SSHI` failed miserably. This is likely because the proposed connectivity was incorrect or the L-S combination didn't properly flip the voltage.

    *   The `SSHI` design is very close. The only problem is ripple on S3.
    *   Ripple $V_{pp}$ is primarily determined by the output capacitor $C_{out}$ and the load current $I_L$.
    *   In S3, $R_L$ is very large ($2.2\text{M}\Omega$), so the load current is small. Why is the ripple high?
    *   Wait, the ripple is measured over 0.7-0.8s. With a light load, the output voltage settles near the Zener clamp ($V_z = 3.3\text{V}$). If the Zener is clamping, the ripple is the difference between the clamp level and the valley. Or, more likely, the L-C resonance from the SSHI is leaking into the output or the charging pulses are too large for the output capacitor to smooth.
    *   To reduce ripple, we can increase $C_{out}$. However, $C_{out}$ in the current best is $8.56\text{uF}$. Let's check the limit: $4.7\text{e-05}$ F ($47\text{uF}$). The current best uses $856\text{nF}$. Increasing $C_{out}$ should reduce ripple.
    *   Wait, if the automatic tuner already tried to optimize $C_{out}$ and it's still failing S3 ripple, maybe the topology needs a slight change to prevent voltage spikes or to better regulate.
    *   S3 is a light load, so the output voltage is high. The Zener $DZ33$ is active. The ripple $V_{pp}$ is probably the "sawtooth" from the charging pulses.

    *   The current `SSHI` is a standard Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor.
    *   Topology:
        `L1` (pzp, n1), `S1` (n1, pzn), `G1` (SYNC).
        `D1-D4` (full bridge).
        `Cout` (out, 0), `Dz` (0, out).
    *   The ripple failure in S3: Light load means $C_{out}$ charges up to $\sim 3.3\text{V}$. The ripple $V_{pp}$ of $64\text{mV}$ is quite small, but slightly above the $50\text{mV}$ limit.
    *   Can we improve this by changing the bridge? Or adding a filter?
    *   Actually, a simple fix for ripple is a larger $C_{out}$. If the tuner didn't reach $47\text{uF}$ or if the ripple is caused by the switching transients passing through the bridge, we might need an LC filter or a different rectification strategy.
    *   However, the `SSHI` is already very efficient.
    *   Let's look at the "Symmetric SSHI" failure. It had two inductors and two switches. The connectivity was:
        `L1 (pzp, n1), S1 (n1, pzn)` and `L2 (pzn, n2), S2 (n2, pzp)`.
        This is meant to flip the voltage in both directions. But it failed completely. Why? Probably because the full bridge `D1-D4` is still there, and the interaction between the symmetric switches and the bridge is problematic, or the phase/ton settings were off.

    *   S3 ripple is the only failure.
    *   In S3, $V_{out}$ is high. The Zener $DZ33$ is clamping.
    *   The ripple is the peak-to-peak variation.
    *   If we increase $C_{out}$, the ripple should decrease.
    *   If the tuner already tried $C_{out} = 47\text{uF}$ and it didn't work, we need a different approach. But looking at the result `Cout = 8.56e-07`, it's quite small. The tuner might not have pushed it higher because larger $C_{out}$ slows down `tup` (startup time).
    *   S3 `tup` is $0.0319\text{s}$, which is very fast. There is plenty of room to increase $C_{out}$ for S3 without violating $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{s}$.
    *   Wait, the tuner optimizes for *all* conditions. S2 has $t_{up} = 0.104\text{s}$ and S4 has $t_{up} = 0.168\text{s}$. There's still room to increase $C_{out}$ significantly.

    *   Is there a way to make the rectification more efficient or the ripple smaller?
    *   What if we use a half-bridge or a different SSHI variant?
    *   Actually, let's try a "Parallel-SSHI" or a "Buck-boost" like structure? No, that's too complex.
    *   What if we add a small series resistance or a filter?
    *   Let's try a "Modified SSHI" where we use a different bridge or a different switch placement.
    *   Current SSHI: $L$ and $S$ are in series with the piezo.
    *   Another option: SSHI with a different inductor placement.
    *   But the most likely culprit for ripple in S3 is just the value of $C_{out}$ being too low to smooth the pulses when the Zener is clamping.
    *   Wait, if the Zener is clamping at $3.3\text{V}$, and the ripple is $64\text{mV}$, the voltage is swinging between $3.236\text{V}$ and $3.3\text{V}$.
    *   Since I can't just "change a value" (the tuner does that), I need to change the *topology*.
    *   How to change topology to reduce ripple?
        1.  Add an LC filter between the rectifier and the output.
        2.  Change the rectifier to something with lower loss or different timing? (Already using DSCH).
        3.  Use a different switching scheme.

    *   Let's try adding an inductor in series with the output to create a $\pi$-filter ($C_{in} \to L \to C_{out}$).
    *   But we only have 16 components.
    *   Current SSHI components: L1, S1, G1, D1, D2, D3, D4, Cout, Dz (9 components).
    *   Adding an LC filter:
        L_filter (out_rect, out), C_out (out, 0).
        And we'd need a capacitor at the rectifier output: C_rect (out_rect, 0).
    *   This would significantly reduce ripple.

    *   L1: pzp -> n1
    *   S1: n1 -> pzn
    *   G1: SYNC (edges=both)
    *   Full bridge:
        D1: pzp -> n_rect
        D2: pzn -> n_rect
        D3: 0 -> pzp
        D4: 0 -> pzn
    *   Filter:
        L_filt: n_rect -> out
        C_rect: n_rect -> 0
        C_out: out -> 0
        Dz: 0 -> out

    *   Let's refine the filter. A simple $L$-$C$ filter after the rectifier:
        `D1, D2, D3, D4` (bridge) -> `node_rect`
        `L_filt` from `node_rect` to `out`
        `C_out` from `out` to `0`
        `Dz` from `0` to `out`
        Wait, `C_rect` might be needed to provide a path for the current from the bridge. Let's add `C_rect` at `node_rect`.

    *   Total components: L1, S1, G1, D1, D2, D3, D4, L_filt, C_rect, C_out, Dz = 11 components. (Within 16 limit).

    *   Wait, if the $C_{out}$ is the only problem, maybe I can just try a slightly different SSHI structure first. But a filter is the classic way to kill ripple.
    *   Let's check the $C_{out}$ again. $8.56\text{uF}$ is quite small. If I just add a second capacitor in parallel, that's not a topology change. If I add an inductor, it is.

    *   Wait, another idea: maybe the "Symmetric SSHI" failure was just due to the specific values or the `G1/G2` settings?
        `G1: ton=1.57e-05s phase=0 edges=pos`
        `G2: ton=1.57e-05s phase=0 edges=neg`
        This should work in theory. Why did it fail?
        `vavg` was $0.3\text{V}$. That's very low.
        Looking at the `Symmetric_SSHI` components:
        `L1 (pzp, n1), S1 (n1, pzn), L2 (pzn, n2), S2 (n2, pzp)`.
        Wait, this means there are *two* paths for the current.
        At the positive peak, `S1` closes, `L1` flips $C_p$.
        At the negative peak, `S2` closes, `L2` flips $C_p$.
        This is a valid SSHI structure. The failure might be the interaction with the full bridge.

    *   Let's stick to the `SSHI` with a filter, as it's a proven way to reduce ripple.

    *   `L1`, `S1`, `G1` (The SSHI part)
    *   `D1`, `D2`, `D3`, `D4` (Full Bridge)
    *   `L2` (Filter inductor)
    *   `C1` (Pre-filter capacitor)
    *   `C2` (Post-filter capacitor/Storage)
    *   `Dz` (Zener clamp)

    *   Connections:
        `L1`: `pzp` to `n1`
        `S1`: `n1` to `pzn`
        `G1`: `SYNC` (controls `S1`)
        `D1`: `pzp` to `n_rect`
        `D2`: `pzn` to `n_rect`
        `D3`: `0` to `pzp`
        `D4`: `0` to `pzn`
        `L2`: `n_rect` to `out`
        `C1`: `n_rect` to `0`
        `C2`: `out` to `0`
        `Dz`: `0` to `out`

    *   S3 ripple: 64mV. This is *so close* to 50mV.
    *   Maybe I don't need a full filter. Maybe just a larger $C_{out}$? But I can't just specify a larger $C_{out}$. The tuner will find it.
    *   Wait, the tuner *did* try to optimize $C_{out}$. If the best result was $8.56\text{uF}$, it means the tuner thought $8.56\text{uF}$ was the best compromise between ripple, $t_{up}$, and $dv$ (settled).
    *   If the ripple is still $64\text{mV}$ at $8.56\text{uF}$, and $t_{up}$ is $0.03\text{s}$, the tuner should have tried $47\text{uF}$!
    *   Wait, look at the $C_{out}$ value: `8.56e-07` F.
    *   $8.56\text{e-07}$ is $0.856\text{uF}$, NOT $8.56\text{uF}$.
    *   $0.856\text{uF}$ is very small! No wonder the ripple is $64\text{mV}$.
    *   Why didn't the tuner use $47\text{uF}$?
    *   Maybe because $V_{max}$ or $dv$ (settled) failed?
    *   In S3, $V_{avg}$ is $3.39\text{V}$, $V_{max}$ is $3.42\text{V}$.
    *   With a huge capacitor, the ripple would be tiny, but the time to reach $1.8\text{V}$ ($t_{up}$) would increase. But $t_{up}$ is $0.03\text{s}$!
    *   There must be some other reason the tuner stopped at $0.856\text{uF}$.
    *   Let's check `settled`: `dv` is the difference between the mean of $0.6$-$0.7\text{s}$ and $0.7$-$0.8\text{s}$.
    *   If $C_{out}$ is too large, the voltage might still be rising at $0.8\text{s}$, so `dv` would be $> 0.02\text{V}$.
    *   Aha! That's it. The "settled" condition is likely failing for larger $C_{out}$.
    *   So, to reduce ripple *without* increasing the time constant too much, an LC filter is actually a great idea. It decouples the storage capacitor from the charging pulses.

    *   L1: pzp -> n1 (SSHI Inductor)
    *   S1: n1 -> pzn (SSHI Switch)
    *   G1: SYNC
    *   D1: pzp -> n_rect (Bridge)
    *   D2: pzn -> n_rect (Bridge)
    *   D3: 0 -> pzp (Bridge)
    *   D4: 0 -> pzn (Bridge)
    *   L2: n_rect -> out (Filter Inductor)
    *   C1: n_rect -> 0 (Input Cap)
    *   C2: out -> 0 (Output Cap)
    *   Dz: 0 -> out (Zener)

    *   Wait, let's check the current limit. The current source is $50\text{uA}$. The inductor `L2` needs to be small enough not to block the current but large enough to filter.
